use_case: Dam-safety sensor anomaly detection: a machine learning module in the instrumentation data platform flags unusual piezometer, seepage weir, and reservoir and tailwater level patterns for review by dam safety staff
vendor_or_model: Instrumentation SaaS vendor (anomaly detection models trained on the company's own 2018-2026 instrument history)
data_categories: Dam safety instrument readings; reservoir and tailwater levels; rainfall; no personal information; outputs are Confidential and alerts that describe failure modes are treated as CEII
human_in_the_loop: Advisory only. Alerts go to a dam safety technician, who checks the instrument and trend; the Chief Dam Safety Engineer decides any action, 12.10 report, or EAP step. Manual weekly trigger-point review continues and cannot be reduced without re-approval
applicable_laws: 18 CFR 12.10(a) and 12.3(b)(4)(viii) (unusual instrumentation readings must be reported; AI output does not change the duty); 18 CFR 12.51 (instrumentation satisfactory to the Regional Engineer); FERC Security Program Rev. 3A 3.2 (trigger points for action); FTC Act Section 5 (vendor claims)
status: Pilot in shadow mode since 2026-04; approved with conditions 2026-08-31; no change to manual reviews

use_case: General-purpose generative AI assistants used by staff to draft letters, procedures, and reports
vendor_or_model: Public chatbots (observed); enterprise assistant in the productivity suite (under evaluation)
data_categories: Risk of CEII, security details, and employee personal information being entered
human_in_the_loop: Human writes and approves every output; tool never connected to OT systems or the CEII library
applicable_laws: CEII handling (POL-04; 18 CFR 388.113 for CEII filed with FERC); FERC Security Program Rev. 3A 3.2 (OPSEC); Fla. Stat. 501.171 if employee personal information leaks
status: Public chatbots prohibited for Restricted or Confidential data (POL-05 4.8); enterprise assistant evaluation due 2026-12-31
